standard_prerequisites.name: Derived completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal is given by the derived Hom from a fixed bounded complex, and by the finite cohomological dimension statement that complex may be taken of finite projective dimension
standard_prerequisites.use: Replaces the completion functor by a Hom complex from a bounded complex of projectives, which is the object whose filtration is studied.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Hom complex from a bounded complex of projectives into a complex represents the derived Hom, and applying it to a filtered complex produces a filtered complex with the induced filtration
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the complex representing the completion together with the filtration whose spectral sequence is the one claimed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The spectral sequence of a filtered complex has the stated first page and differential bidegree, and for a finite filtration on each term it is bounded and converges to the cohomology of the whole complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the identification of the first page with the cohomology of the completion of the graded pieces and the convergence statement.

core_obligations: Use the description of derived completion as a derived Hom from a fixed object and the finite cohomological dimension statement to choose a bounded complex of projective modules, of finite projective dimension, representing that object (proof lines 26569-26573).

Form the Hom complex from that bounded complex of projectives into the given filtered complex, which represents the completion, and equip it with the filtration induced from the given one (proof lines 26574-26579).

Check that the pieces of the filtration represent the completions of the pieces of the given filtration, hence that the associated graded of the new complex represents the completion of the associated graded of the original complex (proof lines 26579-26581).

Obtain the spectral sequence by applying the spectral sequence of a filtered complex to this filtered complex, which gives the stated differential bidegree and first page, and deduce convergence from the finiteness of the filtration on each term, which follows because the complex of projectives is bounded (proof lines 26581-26590).
proof_roadmap: Replace completion by a Hom complex from a bounded complex of projectives of finite projective dimension (proof lines 26569-26573).
Induce the filtration on that complex and identify the associated graded with the completion of the graded pieces (proof lines 26574-26581).
Apply the spectral sequence of a filtered complex and deduce boundedness and convergence from the finiteness of the filtration (proof lines 26581-26590).
difficulty_reason: The statement produces a canonical spectral sequence of derived complete modules for a filtered complex, with first page given by the cohomology of the completions of the graded pieces, and states that it is bounded and converges to the cohomology of the completion when the filtration on each term is finite (statement lines 26555-26567). The proof represents completion as a Hom complex from a bounded complex of projectives of finite projective dimension, which requires the finite cohomological dimension statement, induces the filtration on that Hom complex, verifies that its associated graded computes the completion of the graded pieces, and then invokes the spectral sequence of a filtered complex together with the finiteness of the filtration, which follows from boundedness of the complex of projectives (proof lines 26569-26590). The identification of the associated graded is the step that ties the first page to the completion of the graded pieces.
